Medicare.text: • Changes in Medicare Reimbursement and Regulatory Requirements for Operating IRFs . On April 11, 2025, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (“CMS”) released its notice of proposed rulemaking for fiscal year 2026 for IRFs (the “2026 Proposed Rule”) under the inpatient rehabilitation facility prospective payment system. The 2026 Proposed Rule will implement a net 2.6% market basket increase (market basket update of 3.4% reduced by a productivity adjustment of 0.8%) effective for discharges between October 1, 2025 and September 30, 2026. The 2026 Proposed Rule also includes changes that impact our hospital-by-hospital base rate for Medicare reimbursement. Such changes include, but are not limited to, revisions to the wage index, updates to outlier payments, and updates to the case-mix group relative weights and average lengths of stay values. Based on our analysis that utilizes the acuity of our patients annualized over a twelve-month period ended March 31, 2025, our experience with outlier payments over this same time frame, and other factors, we believe the 2026 Proposed Rule will result in a net increase to our Medicare payment rates of approximately 2.7% effective October 1, 2025.

tax.text:
We provide for income taxes using the asset and liability method. See Note 1, Summary of Significant Accounting Policies , “Income Taxes,” and Note 14, Income Taxes , to the accompanying consolidated financial statements for a more complete discussion of income taxes and our policies related to income taxes.

The application of income tax law is inherently complex. Laws and regulations in this area are voluminous and are often ambiguous. We are required to make many subjective assumptions and judgments regarding our income tax exposures. Interpretations of and guidance surrounding income tax laws and regulations change over time. As such, changes in our subjective assumptions and judgments can materially affect amounts recognized in our consolidated financial statements.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Revenues from Medicare and Medicare Advantage represent approximately 82% of total revenues.

For the year ended December 31, 2025 , Medicaid payments for specific discharges represented only 3.1% of our cons olidated Net operating revenues , and Medicaid discharges represented 5.4% of our total inpatient discharges.
Our free cash flow is the primary source of funding for the considerable investment in our de novo and bed addition growth plans.
We also depend on referrals from physicians, acute-care hospitals, and other healthcare providers in the communities we serve.

Our growth and profitability depend on our ability to establish and maintain close working relationships with patient referral sources and to increase awareness and acceptance of the benefits of inpatient rehabilitation care by our referral sources and their patients.
We also depend on the available labor pool of semi-skilled and unskilled employees in each of the markets in which we operate.
While we do not employ physicians, we do rely on the availability of physicians to treat patients in our hospitals.
Our primary sources of liquidity are cash on hand, cash flows from operations, and borrowings under our revolving credit facility.
The collection of outstanding receivables from third-party payors and patients is our primary source of cash and is critical to our operating performance.
